A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, algorithms, Figures 1–8, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite pagination and citation-number changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and real-data experiments, including approximation accuracy, numerical stability, sampling performance, and computational costs in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 5, Figures 1–8, and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The involutive-MCMC IRF and inverse constructions in Section 3 and Appendix B are unchanged, as are the four flow families and their sampling and density-evaluation procedures in Section 4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four synthetic targets—Banana, Funnel, Cross, and warped Gaussian—and the same real-data models: TReg, Brownian, SparseReg, and LGCP.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain RealNVP, NSF, NUTS, the mean-field Gaussian, and the same MCMC and flow variants. The newly discussed DAIS/DSMC literature introduces no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same metrics, sample counts, flow lengths, training budgets, and reference-estimation procedures, including 50,000-step normalizing-flow training and the 4096-particle AIS procedure.

E4.justification: The inversion-stability and MH-correction analyses in Figures 1–2, comparisons of flow dynamics in Appendix E.1.1, and ensemble-size versus flow-length analysis in Appendix E.1.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including 32-run IRF summaries, 10-run normalizing-flow boxplots, standard-deviation bands, and the 10-run AIS reference estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 1–8 retain identical plotted results, and the accompanying numerical statements, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Assumption 2.2, the convergence theorems, and the definitions, derivations, and proofs in Appendices C–D are unchanged. The added discussion of prior methods' assumptions introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, three listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about invertible measure-preserving constructions, three new variational families, weaker convergence assumptions, and competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: Section 1 newly interprets DAIS/DSMC as kernel tuning and discusses limitations involving idealized transitions, diminishing stepsizes, optimal tuning, and tuning costs. Interpretations of this paper's experiments and the flow limitations in Section 4.5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same code-access statement, hardware information, flow architectures, hyperparameters, and implementation details. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1 adds a focused DAIS/DSMC discussion supported by 13 new references, numbered 26–38 in v3. It also changes the attribution of earlier MixFlow work from 'the first' asymptotically exact variational family to 'an' asymptotically exact variational family.

P1.justification: The introduction gains one substantive paragraph and a revised MixFlow attribution sentence. The section and appendix organization remains intact; other textual differences largely reflect citation renumbering and text reflow.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from PDF page 10 to page 11, appearing after the references have begun, with accompanying text and footnote reflow. All eight figures retain their panels, axes, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: Section 1 provides broader VI–MCMC context and more cautious historical attribution for MixFlow, modestly improving scholarly framing. Figure 4's placement within the references is a small presentation cost. The methods, proofs, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
